correctness.rationale: The exact covariance sum follows from independent common-covariance gradient noise. Commuting deterministic factors make earlier-noise contributions order-invariant under adjacent swaps; direct expansion gives alpha beta (beta-alpha)T(HQ+QH)T. For every PSD W commuting with the SPD H, the trace is twice alpha beta (beta-alpha)trace(WHT^2Q), nonnegative except the scalar swap sign by PSD matrix trace positivity. Adjacent inversions sort globally; strictness needs positive-definite W/Q and a nonzero suffix. Loewner ordering is stated only when HQ+QH is PSD, and the indefinite two-dimensional counterexample is exact. A directly executed NumPy script completed 7,825 formula/risk checks and 6,900 strict alternative-permutation comparisons. No finite enumeration was used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result exactly resolves the fixed-multiset step-ordering problem for terminal noisy quadratic optimization, not merely a selected finite instance. It simultaneously orders every Hessian-spectral quadratic risk for arbitrary anisotropic noise covariance and reveals a sharp boundary between trace and Loewner covariance order. An exact two-eigenvalue spectral-root family proves the high-frequency-first versus noise-optimal objective-cost ratio grows as approximately 2 times the condition number, while deterministic final bias is identical and zero. Thus it exposes an economically and mathematically consequential tradeoff between transient stability and terminal noise.
